def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix
$\hbar>0$ and an integer $d\ge1$, and work in the complex Hilbert space
$L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\overline g$ linear in the first
argument ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).

**Weak derivatives.** For $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ and
$j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$, say that the $j$-th weak derivative of $f$ exists in
$L^2$ when there is a class $g\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ with
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\,D_j\varphi=(-1)\int_{\mathbb R^d}g\,\varphi \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d),$$
where $D_j\varphi$ is the classical partial derivative and the pairing is
bilinear without conjugation ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]).
Such a $g$ is unique as an $L^2$ class
([[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]]); write $D_jf:=g$.
The Sobolev space $W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ is the set of classes
$f\in L^2$ for which $D_1f,\dots,D_df$ all exist in $L^2$, and
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ is the set of $f\in W^{1,2}$ with
$D_jf\in W^{1,2}$ for every $j$, with $D_jD_kf$ written for the iterated
derivative ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).

**(a) Position operators.** For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ define
$$D(Q_j):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C):\ x\mapsto x_jf(x)\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)\},\qquad (Q_jf)(x):=x_jf(x).$$
Thus $Q_jf$ is the class of the pointwise product with the $j$-th coordinate
function.

**(b) Momentum operators.** For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ define
$$D(P_j):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C):\ D_jf\text{ exists in }L^2\},\qquad P_jf:=-i\hbar\,D_jf .$$

Both $Q_j$ and $P_j$ are densely defined $\mathbb C$-linear operators in
$L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$: for $Q_j$ the compactly supported smooth
classes lie in the domain because $x_j$ is bounded there, and for $P_j$ they
lie in the domain because their classical derivatives are weak derivatives in
$L^2$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). For a class
$f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ one has $Q_jf=x_jf$ and
$P_jf=-i\hbar\,\partial_jf$ pointwise. The self-adjointness of these operators
and their Fourier representation are proved in
the companion self-adjointness lemma on this page, not
asserted here; for $d=1$ the domain $D(P)$ of the single momentum operator
coincides with $W^{1,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$.
lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-weak-pro:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $d\ge1$
and let $a\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ be a class having weak first
derivatives $D_ja\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ for every
$j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$, in the sense of
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Let
$u\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).
Then $au\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ and, for every $j$,
$$D_j(au)=a\,D_ju+(D_ja)\,u \qquad\text{as }L^2\text{ classes,}$$
with pointwise products of chosen representatives. No boundedness of $u$ is
assumed.
lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, and let $Q_j,P_j$ be the position and momentum operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] on
$L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$; let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel
transform with $\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$
on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]).

(a) For every $j$, $Q_j$ is self-adjoint with domain
$D(Q_j)=\{f\in L^2:\ x_jf\in L^2\}$.

(b) For every $j$, $P_j$ is self-adjoint with domain
$$D(P_j)=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C):\ \xi_j\mathcal F_2f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_j)$, $\mathcal F_2(P_jf)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_j\,\mathcal F_2f(\xi)$
for almost every $\xi$. In particular $P_jf=-i\hbar D_jf$ for every
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$, and for $d=1$ the domain of the single
momentum operator is exactly $D(P)=W^{1,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$.

(c) For every $a\in\mathbb R^d$ the translation $(T_af)(x):=f(x-a)$ is a
unitary operator, $T_aD(P_j)=D(P_j)$, $T_aP_jT_a^{-1}=P_j$,
$T_aD(Q_j)=D(Q_j)$ and $T_aQ_jT_a^{-1}=Q_j-a_j$ for every $j$; moreover
$D_j(T_af)=T_a(D_jf)$ as $L^2$ classes for every $f\in W^{1,2}$, so $T_a$
preserves $W^{1,2}$ and $W^{2,2}$.
def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$, $m>0$ and
$q\in\mathbb R$, and work on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with the position
and momentum operators $Q_j,P_j$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]].

**Admissible magnetic data.** Call the pair $(A,\Phi)$ **admissible** when
$A=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$ is a triple of real-valued classes
$A_j\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ having weak first derivatives
$D_kA_j\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ for all $j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$, and
$\Phi\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ is a real-valued bounded class
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Write $|A|^2:=A_1^2+A_2^2+A_3^2$
and $\operatorname{div}A:=D_1A_1+D_2A_2+D_3A_3$ for chosen representatives;
both are bounded classes.

**Magnetic momentum operators.** For admissible $(A,\Phi)$ and
$j\in\{1,2,3\}$ define the $\mathbb C$-linear operator
$$P_{A,j}:=P_j-qA_j,\qquad D(P_{A,j}):=D(P_j)=\{f\in L^2:\ D_jf\in L^2\},$$
where $A_j$ acts as multiplication; this is well defined into $L^2$ because
$A_j\in L^\infty$ and $f\in L^2$. The self-adjointness of $P_{A,j}$ is proved
later on this page, not asserted here.

**The operator.** Put $D(K_{A,\Phi}):=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and
$$K_{A,\Phi}u:=\frac1{2m}\sum_{j=1}^3P_{A,j}\bigl(P_{A,j}u\bigr)+q\,\Phi u \qquad(u\in D(K_{A,\Phi})).$$
This is well defined: if $u\in W^{2,2}$ and $(A,\Phi)$ is admissible, then
$P_{A,j}u=P_ju-qA_ju\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ by
[[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-weak-product-rule]] together with
$P_ju\in W^{1,2}$, so $P_{A,j}u\in D(P_{A,j})$ and every summand lies in
$L^2$. Write $K_0:=K_{(0,0)}$ for the **free operator**, so that
$K_0u=\frac1{2m}\sum_jP_j(P_ju)$ on $W^{2,2}$. The same formula shows
$K_{A,\Phi}$ is $\mathbb C$-linear. Its symmetry, self-adjointness, expansion
in the magnetic momenta and relative boundedness with respect to $K_0$ are the
content of
the self-adjointness theorem on this page,
not asserted here.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-bounded-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$, $m>0$,
$q\in\mathbb R$ and an admissible pair $(A,\Phi)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]], and let
$P_{A,j}$, $K_{A,\Phi}$ and $K_0$ be the operators defined there on
$L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$. Then:

(a) for every $j$, $P_{A,j}=P_j-qA_j$ is self-adjoint with domain
$D(P_{A,j})=D(P_j)=\{f: D_jf\in L^2\}$; and for every
$u\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ one has $P_{A,j}u\in W^{1,2}$ and
$P_{A,j}u=P_ju-qA_ju$;

(b) for every $u\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ the expansion holds:
$$K_{A,\Phi}u=\frac1{2m}P^2u-\frac{q}{2m}\sum_{j=1}^3\bigl(P_jA_j+A_jP_j\bigr)u +\frac{q^2}{2m}|A|^2u+q\,\Phi u,\qquad P^2u:=\sum_{j=1}^3P_j(P_ju)=-\hbar^2\sum_{j=1}^3D_jD_ju,$$
where $(P_jA_j+A_jP_j)u:=P_j(A_ju)+A_jP_ju$, and each term lies in $L^2$;

(c) $K_{A,\Phi}$ is symmetric on its domain and self-adjoint with
$D(K_{A,\Phi})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$;

(d) for every $a\in[0,1)$ there is $b\in[0,\infty)$ with
$$\|(K_{A,\Phi}-K_0)u\|\le a\,\|K_0u\|+b\|u\|\qquad \bigl(u\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\bigr),$$
so $K_{A,\Phi}-K_0$ has $K_0$-bound strictly below one
([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]); consequently
$K_{A,\Phi}$ is bounded below.

The assertion is a statement about the displayed differential expression with
its stated coefficient hypotheses; it identifies no physical field, particle
or measured Hamiltonian.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-h2:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$, $m>0$,
$q\in\mathbb R$, an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, admissible magnetic
data $(A,\Phi)$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and a real function
$\chi:\mathbb R^3\times I\to\mathbb R$ such that:

1. for every $t\in I$, $\chi(\cdot,t)$ is $C^2$ on $\mathbb R^3$, and the
   functions $D_j\chi(\cdot,t)$, $D_kD_j\chi(\cdot,t)$ are bounded on
   $\mathbb R^3$ with bounds independent of $t\in I$;
2. for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, $t\mapsto\chi(x,t)$ is differentiable on $I$,
   and $\partial_t\chi$ is bounded on $\mathbb R^3\times I$.

Put $\theta(x,t):=\frac{q}{\hbar}\chi(x,t)$ and let
$G(t):L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\to L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be
multiplication by $e^{i\theta(\cdot,t)}$ ([[def-complex-exponential]]).
Then for every $t\in I$:

(a) $G(t)$ is unitary and preserves $W^{1,2}$ and $W^{2,2}$:
$G(t)W^{k,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)=W^{k,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ for
$k=1,2$;

(b) for every $u\in W^{1,2}$ and every $j$,
$$D_j(G(t)u)=G(t)D_ju+i\,(D_j\theta(\cdot,t))\,G(t)u \qquad\text{as }L^2\text{ classes};$$

(c) for every $u\in W^{1,2}$ the gauge covariance identity holds:
$$\bigl(P_j-q(A_j+D_j\chi(\cdot,t))\bigr)G(t)u=G(t)\bigl(P_j-qA_j\bigr)u;$$

(d) $t\mapsto G(t)h$ is continuous on $I$ for every $h\in L^2$, and for every
$h\in L^2$ and $t\in I$ the difference quotients converge in $L^2$:
$$\lim_{s\to0}\frac1s\bigl(G(t+s)h-G(t)h\bigr) =\frac{iq}{\hbar}\,\bigl(\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t)\bigr)\,G(t)h .$$

The function $\chi$ is an arbitrary function with the stated regularity; no
identification with a physical gauge choice is asserted.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-tr:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$, $m>0$,
$q\in\mathbb R$, admissible magnetic data $(A,\Phi)$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and a
gauge function $\chi:\mathbb R^3\times I\to\mathbb R$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-h2-domain-preservation]], with
underlying open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. Put
$A'_j(\cdot,t):=A_j+D_j\chi(\cdot,t)$, $\Phi'(\cdot,t):=\Phi-\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t)$
and, for $t\in I$,
$$H'(t):=K_{A'(t),\Phi'(t)},\qquad G(t):=\text{multiplication by }e^{i\frac q\hbar\chi(\cdot,t)} ,$$
so that $(A'(t),\Phi'(t))$ is admissible for every $t$ and $H'(t)$ is
self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ by
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-bounded-coefficient-magnetic-operator]].
Let $K:=K_{A,\Phi}$ and $U(\tau):=e^{-i\tau K/\hbar}$ for $\tau\in\mathbb R$,
the strongly continuous unitary group generated by $-iK/\hbar$
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]).

(a) For every $t\in I$ one has the operator identity on $W^{2,2}$
$$H'(t)=G(t)\,K\,G(t)^{-1}-q\,\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t),$$
where the last term is multiplication by $-q\,\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t)$;
explicitly, $G(t)KG(t)^{-1}=K_{A'(t),\Phi}$ is the magnetic operator with the
transported vector potential and the original scalar potential $\Phi$.

(b) For every $u_0\in W^{2,2}$ and $s\in I$ the curve
$$u(t):=G(t)\,U(t-s)\,G(s)^{-1}u_0\qquad(t\in I)$$
lies in $W^{2,2}$ for every $t$, is differentiable into $L^2$ on $I$, and
satisfies $u(s)=u_0$ and $i\hbar\,u'(t)=H'(t)u(t)$ for every $t\in I$. It is
the unique such curve: if $v:I\to W^{2,2}$ is continuous into
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, differentiable into $L^2$, with
$i\hbar\,v'(t)=H'(t)v(t)$ for all $t$ and $v(s)=u_0$, then $v=u$.

(c) The two-parameter family
$$U'(t,s):=G(t)\,U(t-s)\,G(s)^{-1}\qquad(t,s\in I)$$
consists of unitary operators mapping $W^{2,2}$ onto $W^{2,2}$, satisfies
$U'(t,t)=I$ and the composition law
$U'(t,r)U'(r,s)=U'(t,s)$ for all $t,r,s\in I$, and
$u(t)=U'(t,s)u_0$ is the solution of (b).

The theorem provides dynamics for the transformed coefficient class only; it
asserts no general well-posedness for arbitrary time-dependent unbounded
generators.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-smooth-l:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix
$\hbar>0$, $m>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be nonempty open sets, let $V:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be
continuous and let $\psi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb C$ be such that $\psi$,
$\partial_t\psi$ and all spatial partial derivatives $\partial_j\psi$,
$\partial_k\partial_j\psi$ ($j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) exist and are continuous on
$\Omega\times I$, and
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi(x,t)=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta\psi(x,t)+V(x)\psi(x,t) \qquad\text{for every }(x,t)\in\Omega\times I,$$
where $\Delta$ is the Laplacian ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Define the **current**
$$j(x,t):=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{\psi(x,t)}\,\nabla\psi(x,t)\bigr)\in\mathbb R^3 .$$
Then:

(a) *pointwise continuity equation.* For every $(x,t)\in\Omega\times I$,
$$\partial_t|\psi|^2(x,t)+\operatorname{div}j(x,t)=0,$$
where the divergence is the classical one of the $C^1$ field
$x\mapsto j(x,t)$ ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]);

(b) *integrated balance.* If $D\subseteq\Omega$ is a bounded open set with
$C^1$ boundary and $\overline D\subseteq\Omega$
([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]), then
$t\mapsto\int_D|\psi(x,t)|^2dx$ is differentiable on $I$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_D|\psi(x,t)|^2dx=-\int_{\partial D}j(x,t)\cdot n(x)\,dS ,$$
$n$ the outward unit normal;

(c) *global conservation under domination.* If $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, if there
is $g\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ with $|\psi(x,t)|^2\le g(x)$ for almost every $x$
and every $t\in I$, and if
$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\ \sup_{t\in I}\ \int_{\{|x|=R\}}|j(x,t)|\,dS=0,$$
then $t\mapsto\|\psi(\cdot,t)\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}^2$ is constant on $I$;

(d) *norm conservation from unitary dynamics.* If $K$ is a self-adjoint
operator on a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and
$\psi(t):=e^{-itK/\hbar}\psi_0$ for some $\psi_0\in\mathcal H$, then
$\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi_0\|$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]).

Assertion (d) is independent of the smooth local model of (a)-(c); no
interpretation of $|\psi|^2$ as a measured counting rate is asserted.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-coherent:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(D,\mathcal A,dx)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space, let $L^2(D)$ be the
complex Hilbert space of
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]], and let
$a,b\in L^2(D)$.

(a) *Coherent law.* If $a+b\ne0$ as a class, i.e. $\|a+b\|>0$, then
$$p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B):=\frac{\displaystyle\int_B|a+b|^2\,dx}{\|a+b\|^2}, \qquad B\in\mathcal A,$$
defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$
([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]), and for every $B$
$$\int_B|a+b|^2dx=\int_B|a|^2dx+\int_B|b|^2dx+2\operatorname{Re}\int_Ba\overline b\,dx .$$

(b) *Incoherent law.* If $a\ne0$, $b\ne0$ and $w\in[0,1]$, then
$$p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_B|a|^2dx}{\|a\|^2} +(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_B|b|^2dx}{\|b\|^2}$$
defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$.

(c) *Signed difference.* Let $a,b$ be unit vectors with
$\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle\ne-1$, and put
$$N(B):=\int_B\bigl(|a|^2+|b|^2\bigr)dx,\qquad c(B):=\operatorname{Re}\int_Ba\overline b\,dx,\qquad p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B):=\frac{N(B)+2c(B)}{2+2c(D)},\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=\frac{N(B)}2 .$$
Then for every $B$, $N(B)-2c(B)=\int_B|a-b|^2dx\ge0$, and
$$p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)-p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B) =\frac{2c(B)-c(D)N(B)}{2\bigl(1+c(D)\bigr)} .$$
Equality $p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ for every measurable bin holds exactly when $2\operatorname{Re}(a\overline b)=c(D)(|a|^2+|b|^2)$ almost everywhere. In particular, if $a\perp b$ then $c(D)=0$ and the signed difference is $c(B)$, so orthogonality alone does not imply equality on each bin. If $b=a$ then equality holds on every bin. Coherence of the preparation changes the bin law according to the amplitudes and their actual normalization.

(d) *Marker overlap.* Let $K$ be a complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]) with unit vectors $e_1,e_2$, let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$
with $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1$, let $a,b$ be unit vectors and put
$\Psi:=\alpha\,a\otimes e_1+\beta\,b\otimes e_2$ in the completed tensor
product $L^2(D)\widehat\otimes K$. The reduced weight $\rho:=\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is defined even when $\Psi=0$, with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\|\Psi\|^2$. If $\Psi\ne0$, $B\in\mathcal A$ has finite measure and
$P_B$ is multiplication by $\mathbf 1_B$, then the normalized bin law of the
reduced weight $\rho$ is
$$\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_B)}{\operatorname{tr}\rho} =\frac{1}{\|\Psi\|^2}\int_B\Bigl(|\alpha|^2|a|^2+|\beta|^2|b|^2 +2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\alpha\overline\beta\,\langle e_1,e_2\rangle\, a(x)\overline{b(x)}\bigr)\Bigr)dx,$$
and $|\langle e_1,e_2\rangle|\le1$: the marker overlap bounds the complex cross coefficient in modulus (its phase may rotate the real interference contribution); that contribution vanishes identically when $e_1\perp e_2$, leaving the incoherent
weight. If $\Psi=0$, no normalized law is defined.

(e) *Finite sampling.* If a detector model produces, for a fixed bin $B$,
$N$ independent trials each with success probability $p=p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)$
or $p=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$, and $S_N$ is the number of successes, then $S_N$
is binomial$(N,p)$ and $\mathbb E[S_N/N]=p$,
$\operatorname{Var}(S_N/N)=p(1-p)/N$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-chsh-and-finite-sampling-law]], clause (c)).

All assertions are identities and inequalities for the specified
preparation vectors; no detector law, no measured counting rate and no
empirical claim is asserted, and (e) is conditional on the stated
independent-trials model.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-covarian:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first
argument ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A,B$ be
symmetric densely defined operators on $\mathcal H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let
$u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$ satisfy $\|u\|=1$. Put
$$a:=\langle Au,u\rangle,\quad b:=\langle Bu,u\rangle,\quad x:=(A-a)u,\quad y:=(B-b)u,\quad \Delta A:=\|x\|,\quad\Delta B:=\|y\|,$$
and define the **covariance** of the pair $(A,B)$ in the preparation $u$ by
$\operatorname{Cov}_u(A,B):=\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle$.
Then:

(a) $a,b\in\mathbb R$; $x,y\in\mathcal H$; and
$\operatorname{Cov}_u(A,B)\in\mathbb R$ is symmetric in its two arguments:
$\operatorname{Cov}_u(A,B)=\operatorname{Cov}_u(B,A)$;

(b) *covariance-refined bound:*
$$(\Delta A)^2(\Delta B)^2\ge\bigl[\operatorname{Cov}_u(A,B)\bigr]^2 +\bigl[\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle\bigr]^2 \ge\bigl[\operatorname{Cov}_u(A,B)\bigr]^2,$$
so in particular $\Delta A\,\Delta B\ge|\operatorname{Cov}_u(A,B)|$;

(c) equality holds in (b)'s first inequality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are
linearly dependent (in the convention that $x=0$ or $y=0$ counts as
dependence);

(d) if in addition $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$ — that is $Bu\in D(A)$ and
$Au\in D(B)$ — then the pairing
$\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle:=\langle ABu,u\rangle-\langle BAu,u\rangle$ is
defined and
$$\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle=-2i\,\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle,$$
in particular it is purely imaginary, and consequently
$$(\Delta A)^2(\Delta B)^2\ge\bigl[\operatorname{Cov}_u(A,B)\bigr]^2 +\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|^2, \qquad \Delta A\,\Delta B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr| .$$

Clauses (a)-(c) use no product $AB$ or $BA$ and no assumption on the domains
of such products. The quantities are preparation quantities of the vector $u$;
no measurement model, apparatus error or energy-time interpretation is
asserted.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-maximal-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$ and let
$Q$ and $P$ be the position and momentum operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] on
$L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$; by
[[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]] both are
self-adjoint, $D(P)=W^{1,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and
$D(Q)=\{f:\ xf\in L^2\}$. Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ have $\|f\|=1$, and put
$$a:=\langle Qf,f\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}x|f(x)|^2dx,\qquad b:=\langle Pf,f\rangle,$$
$$x_Q:=(Q-a)f,\qquad y_P:=(P-b)f,\qquad \Delta Q:=\|x_Q\|,\qquad\Delta P:=\|y_P\| .$$
Then:

(a) $a,b\in\mathbb R$, and with $m_1:=\int_{\mathbb R}f'\overline f\,dx$ and
$m_2:=\int_{\mathbb R}xf'\overline f\,dx$ (absolutely convergent complex
integrals, $f'$ the weak derivative) one has
$$\operatorname{Re}m_1=0,\qquad \operatorname{Re}m_2=-\tfrac12,\qquad b=\hbar\,\operatorname{Im}m_1;$$

(b) $\langle x_Q,y_P\rangle=-\frac{i\hbar}2+\hbar\,\operatorname{Im}m_2-ab$;
consequently $\operatorname{Im}\langle x_Q,y_P\rangle=-\frac\hbar2$ and
$$\Delta Q\,\Delta P\ge\frac\hbar2 ;$$

(c) equality $\Delta Q\Delta P=\frac\hbar2$ holds if and only if
$x_Q,y_P$ are linearly dependent and $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_Q,y_P\rangle=0$;

(d) no assumption on the products $QP$ or $PQ$ is used: the assertion holds on
the full maximal domain of the pair, and the means $a,b$, the centered vectors
$x_Q,y_P$ and the variances are finite on it.

The statement concerns a preparation vector only; it asserts no apparatus
error, jointly measured distribution or physical interpretation.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-galilean:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$, $m>0$,
a real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$, and let
$K:=\frac1{2m}\sum_jP_j^2+M_V$ with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
be the free-plus-bounded-potential operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c); write $V_u(x,t):=V(x-ut)$ for $u\in\mathbb R^3$. For $u\in\mathbb R^3$
and $t\in\mathbb R$ define the **boost operator**
$$\bigl(B_u(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=e^{\,i\bigl(\frac m\hbar u\cdot x-\frac{m|u|^2}{2\hbar}t\bigr)}\psi(x-ut), \qquad \psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C).$$
Then:

(a) for every $t$, $B_u(t)$ is unitary with $B_u(t)^{-1}=B_u(t)^*$, and
$B_u(t)$ maps $W^{1,2}$ and $W^{2,2}$ onto themselves;

(b) for every $u_0\in W^{2,2}$ and every $s\in\mathbb R$ the curve
$v(t):=B_u(t)\,e^{-i(t-s)K/\hbar}B_u(s)^{-1}u_0$ lies in $W^{2,2}$, is differentiable into
$L^2$ on $\mathbb R$, and satisfies $v(s)=u_0$ and
$$i\hbar\,v'(t)=\Bigl(\frac1{2m}\sum_jP_j^2+M_{V_u(\cdot,t)}\Bigr)v(t) \qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
where $M_{V_u(\cdot,t)}$ is multiplication by $x\mapsto V(x-ut)$. It is the
unique such curve: if $w:\mathbb R\to W^{2,2}$ is continuous into
$W^{2,2}$, differentiable into $L^2$ and satisfies the same equation with
$w(s)=u_0$, then $w=v$;

(c) the two-parameter family
$U_u(t,s):=B_u(t)\,e^{-i(t-s)K/\hbar}\,B_u(s)^{-1}$ consists of unitaries
preserving $W^{2,2}$, satisfies $U_u(t,t)=I$,
$U_u(t,r)U_u(r,s)=U_u(t,s)$, and $v(t)=U_u(t,s)v_0$ is the solution of (b)
at time $s$ for every $v_0\in W^{2,2}$;

(d) *free propagator covariance.* With $K_0:=\frac1{2m}\sum_jP_j^2$ (that is
$V=0$) one has
$B_u(t)e^{-i(t-s)K_0/\hbar}=e^{-i(t-s)K_0/\hbar}B_u(s)$ for all $t,s$.

All assertions concern the displayed unitary family and the Schrodinger-type
equation; no Lorentz structure, no photon limit and no worldline of an
unmeasured particle is asserted.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conserve:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $K$ be a
self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H$ with spectral projection-valued measure
$E=E_K$ on the Borel subsets of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and put
$U(t):=e^{-itK/\hbar}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE(\lambda)$ for
$\hbar>0$, the strongly continuous unitary group generated by $-iK/\hbar$
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]).

(a) If a bounded operator $B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ satisfies
$BE(C)=E(C)B$ for every Borel set $C\subseteq\mathbb R$, then
$BU(t)=U(t)B$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.

(a') If a bounded self-adjoint operator $S$ satisfies $SK\subseteq KS$ — that
is $S(Kx)=K(Sx)$ for every $x\in D(K)$ — then $SU(t)=U(t)S$ for every $t$.

(b) Let $F$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space
$(Y,\Sigma)$ with $F(S)E(C)=E(C)F(S)$ for all $S\in\Sigma$ and all Borel
$C\subseteq\mathbb R$. Then:

(i) $F(S)U(t)=U(t)F(S)$ for all $t$ and $S$;

(ii) for every density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H$ — a self-adjoint
positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$
([[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)) —
the numbers $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F(S))$ are independent of $t$:
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(U(t)\rho U(t)^*F(S)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F(S)\bigr) \qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ S\in\Sigma);$$

(iii) for every unit vector $\psi\in\mathcal H$ and every $S$,
$\|F(S)U(t)\psi\|^2=\|F(S)\psi\|^2$ for all $t$;

(c) applying (b) with $F=E$: for every density operator $\rho$ the energy law
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(C))$ is independent of $t$, for every unit $\psi$
the law $\|E(C)U(t)\psi\|^2=\|E(C)\psi\|^2$ is independent of $t$, and if
$\psi\in D(K)$ then both existing scalar moments are conserved:
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^k\,dE_{K,U(t)\psi}(\lambda) =\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^k\,dE_{K,\psi}(\lambda),\qquad k=1,2,$$
with the integrals finite at $t=0$ and equal to $\langle K\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $\|K\psi\|^2$ respectively; moments that are infinite at $t=0$ remain
outside the assertion;

(d) if $K\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and unit
$\psi\in D(K)$, then $U(t)\psi=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi$ for every $t$, and
every $S\mapsto\|F(S)\psi\|^2$ of (b) agrees with
$S\mapsto\|F(S)U(t)\psi\|^2$.

No equilibration, relaxation or convergence of the law of an arbitrary state
is asserted, and no moment beyond those finite at $t=0$ is claimed.
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-graph-do:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), let $K,A$ be self-adjoint operators on $\mathcal H$,
let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, fix $\hbar>0$ and let
$\psi:I\to\mathcal H$ satisfy, for every $t\in I$:

1. $\psi(t)\in D(A)$, and the curve is $C^1$ **into $D(A)$ with the graph
   norm** of $A$ ([[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]],
   [[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]]), meaning that both
   $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ and $t\mapsto A\psi(t)$ are $C^1$ into $\mathcal H$;
2. $K\psi(t)\in D(A)$, that is $\psi(t)\in D(AK)$; the additional condition
   $A\psi(t)\in D(K)$ (that is $\psi(t)\in D(KA)$) is imposed only in the
   clauses that state it;
3. $\psi'(t)=-\frac i\hbar K\psi(t)$ in $\mathcal H$.

Then, writing $f(t):=\langle A\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ and
$(KA-AK)\psi:=K(A\psi)-A(K\psi)$ for $\psi\in D(AK)\cap D(KA)$:

(a) if hypotheses 1 and 3 and $K\psi(t)\in D(A)$ for all $t$ hold (that is,
$\psi(t)\in D(AK)$), then $f$ is $C^1$ on $I$ and
$$f'(t)=-\frac2\hbar\operatorname{Im}\bigl\langle A\psi(t),K\psi(t)\bigr\rangle ;$$
if moreover $A\psi(t)\in D(K)$ for all $t$ (that is, $\psi(t)\in D(KA)$), then
also $f'(t)=\frac i\hbar\langle(KA-AK)\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$;

(b) if $(A_t)_{t\in I}$ is a family of bounded self-adjoint operators that is
$C^1$ in operator norm and $\psi$ satisfies 1 and 3 above (no product-domain
hypothesis), then $g(t):=\langle A_t\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ is $C^1$ with
$$g'(t)=\langle A'_t\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle -\frac2\hbar\operatorname{Im}\bigl\langle A_t\psi(t),K\psi(t)\bigr\rangle ;$$
if in addition $A_t\psi(t)\in D(K)$ and $K\psi(t)\in D(A_t)$ for all $t$,
then this equals
$\langle A'_t\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle+\frac i\hbar\langle[K,A_t]\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$;

(c) if moreover $\|\psi(t)\|=1$ for all $t$ and for a fixed self-adjoint $A$
as in (a) one has $f'(t_0)\ne0$ at some $t_0\in I$, then with the preparation
spreads
$$\Delta K(t_0):=\bigl\|(K-\langle K\psi(t_0),\psi(t_0)\rangle)\psi(t_0)\bigr\|, \qquad \Delta A(t_0):=\bigl\|(A-f(t_0))\psi(t_0)\bigr\|,$$
and the timescale $\tau_A(t_0):=\Delta A(t_0)/|f'(t_0)|$, the bound
$$\Delta K(t_0)\,\tau_A(t_0)\ge\frac\hbar2$$
holds;

(d) if $f'(t_0)=0$ then the definition of $\tau_A(t_0)$ supplies no timescale,
and no universal time operator, apparatus error or energy-time observable is
asserted by (a)-(c).
thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conditio:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$, $m>0$,
$\gamma_s\in\mathbb R$ and a real function $B_z\in C^1(\mathbb R)$ with
$B_z$ and $B_z'$ bounded. Let
$$\mathcal H:=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\oplus L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C), \qquad \langle(u_+,u_-),(v_+,v_-)\rangle:=\langle u_+,v_+\rangle+\langle u_-,v_-\rangle,$$
let $P_j,Q_j$ act componentwise ([[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]],
[[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]]), write
$B_z(Q_x)$ for componentwise multiplication by $x\mapsto B_z(x_1)$ and
$$S_z(u_+,u_-):=\Bigl(\frac\hbar2u_+,-\frac\hbar2u_-\Bigr),\qquad K(u_+,u_-):=\Bigl(\frac1{2m}\sum_jP_j^2u_+-\frac{\gamma_s\hbar}2B_z(Q_x)u_+,\ \frac1{2m}\sum_jP_j^2u_-+\frac{\gamma_s\hbar}2B_z(Q_x)u_-\Bigr),$$
with $D(K):=\{(u_+,u_-):u_+,u_-\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\}$, so that
formally $K=\frac1{2m}\sum_jP_j^2-\gamma_sS_zB_z(Q_x)$. Identify the spin
factor with $V_{1/2}=\mathbb C^2$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] by the basis
$(e_{1/2},e_{-1/2})$, so that on that factor $S_z=\hbar J_z$ with
$J_ze_m=me_m$ and eigenvalues $\pm\hbar/2$. Then:

(a) $K$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(K)$, and $S_zK=KS_z$ on $D(K)$;
consequently, for $u(t):=e^{-itK/\hbar}u_0$ and the sector projections
$p_\pm:=\frac12(I\pm\frac2\hbar S_z)$,
$$\|p_\pm u(t)\|^2=\|p_\pm u_0\|^2,\qquad \langle S_zu(t),u(t)\rangle=\langle S_zu_0,u_0\rangle \qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ u_0\in\mathcal H);$$

(b) for every $u_0\in D(K^2):=\{u\in D(K):Ku\in D(K)\}$ the function
$t\mapsto\langle P_xu(t),u(t)\rangle$ is $C^1$ and
$$\frac d{dt}\langle P_xu(t),u(t)\rangle =\gamma_s\,\bigl\langle S_zB_z'(Q_x)u(t),u(t)\bigr\rangle,$$
where $B_z'(Q_x)$ is componentwise multiplication by $x\mapsto B_z'(x_1)$ and
$S_zB_z'(Q_x)(u_+,u_-)=(\frac\hbar2B_z'(Q_x)u_+,-\frac\hbar2B_z'(Q_x)u_-)$;

(c) if in addition $\|u_0\|=1$, $p_+u_0=u_0$, and $B_z'(s)=G$ for every
$s$ in a Borel set $N\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$\int_{\mathbb R\setminus N}\eta_+(x_1)\,dx_1=0$, where $\eta_+(x_1):=\int_{\mathbb R^2}|u_0^+(x_1,x_2,x_3)|^2\,dx_2\,dx_3$ is the first-coordinate marginal density, then
$$\frac d{dt}\Bigr|_{t=0}\langle P_xu(t),u(t)\rangle=\frac{\gamma_s\hbar}2G,$$
an identity at the preparation time $t=0$; for $t\ne0$ the general formula of
(b) applies and may differ;

(d) for the model field $B(x):=(0,0,B_z(x_1))$ one has
$\operatorname{div}B=0$ and
$\operatorname{curl}B=(0,-B_z'(x_1),0)$ at every point.

The statements are conditional identities for the displayed model; no
apparatus, measured trajectory, source-free Maxwell realisation of $B$ or
inference about an individual particle is asserted.
